title: PM Fils-Aimé Departs for Vatican and Rome Amid Criticism That Gangs Are Advancing While PM Accumulates Foreign Trips
detail: Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé departed Haiti on May 8, 2026 at the head of a high-level government delegation for an official diplomatic mission to Rome and the Holy See, scheduled to run through May 11. The mission's stated objectives include strengthening diplomatic ties, consolidating humanitarian and development cooperation with the Vatican and Italian institutions, and what Haitian government sources described as 'spiritual mobilization' for peace in Haiti. The PM is expected to meet with Holy See officials, potentially including a papal audience, as well as representatives of international organizations based in Rome including the FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) and IFAD (International Fund for Agricultural Development) — both relevant to Haiti's acute food security crisis. The Vatican's Catholic Church network in Haiti operates approximately 300 schools and 50 health facilities, making it one of the most significant service providers remaining functional in gang-affected communities. The departure drew criticism from Haitian-language media and civil society: Rezo Nòdwès published commentary noting that 'gangs are gaining ground while Fils-Aimé is collecting foreign trips,' pointing to the simultaneous Viv Ansanm destruction of the Marchand-Dessalines police station on May 7 and Artibonite gang expansion. The Vatican trip follows PM Fils-Aimé's CNN/Amanpour interview on May 1, an official diplomatic presence at the UN General Assembly earlier in 2026, and multiple other international appearances — reflecting a deliberate strategy of intensive foreign engagement to consolidate support ahead of the planned August 30, 2026 elections. The PM's absence during the current Artibonite escalation is a politically sensitive point for the Haitian government.

media.caption: PM Fils-Aimé departs for Vatican and Rome diplomatic mission May 8–11, 2026, as Haitian media criticizes the trip amid Artibonite gang escalation

title: Moïse Assassination Trial Jury Continues Deliberations; Verdict Expected in Miami Federal Court
detail: The jury in the Jovenel Moïse assassination trial continued deliberations on May 8, 2026, at the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida in Miami. Jury deliberations began on May 6 after closing arguments were delivered by prosecution and defense on May 4–5. The jury deliberated for at least one full day on May 6 without reaching a verdict, with proceedings ongoing as of May 8. The four defendants — Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages — face charges related to conspiracy to commit murder and other crimes connected to the July 7, 2021 killing of President Moïse at his private residence in Pétion-Ville. Intriago, a Florida-based Venezuelan-American businessman, is alleged to have been a primary financier of the operation. James Solages, a Haitian-American with prior US security service connections, is alleged to have participated directly in the attack team. The trial has drawn extensive Haitian diaspora interest and media coverage in South Florida, which has the second-largest Haitian diaspora population in the United States. A conviction would represent a partial accountability milestone for a crime that directly triggered Haiti's governance collapse and the gang takeover that followed. However, the question of who ordered the assassination — believed to involve higher-level political and business figures not yet prosecuted — remains open. Haitian civil society organizations monitoring the trial emphasized that justice for Moïse requires prosecuting the masterminds, not only the direct operatives.

media.caption: Moïse assassination jury deliberations continue at Miami federal court — verdict pending on four defendants charged in the 2021 killing
